categories.title: Ritual and temple
categories.blurb: Dance offered before an image or a fire: the temple traditions of India and Southeast Asia, the masked processions of Japan and Tibet, and the trance forms that carry a body out of its own voice.

categories.title: Court and classical stage
categories.blurb: The forms a court paid for: ballet from the Italian halls to the Russian stage, the theatre dances of Japan and Java, and the modern schools that broke the story in order to keep the body.

categories.title: Folk and national
categories.blurb: What a village does at a wedding, a harvest or a saint's day — and what a nation later adopts as its own face. The steps are old, the borders on them are new.

categories.title: Social and partner
categories.blurb: Two people, one room, a band: the couple dances a city invents when it has a night off — from the Viennese ballroom to the Caribbean port, and the codes that decide who may ask whom.

categories.title: Street and club
categories.blurb: The forms made by people with a pavement and a record player: the Bronx, Los Angeles, Kingston, Lagos, Johannesburg. No school fees, a name given on the floor, and a battle instead of an exam.

categories.title: Martial arts of East Asia
categories.blurb: The other half of the same training: a form rehearsed until the body forgets it is deciding. Japan's schools, China's families and Korea's national sports, each with the century it was founded.

categories.title: Martial arts of South and Southeast Asia
categories.blurb: Empty hand, stick, blade and rope, taught in a kalari, a village square or a temple courtyard: Kerala's gymnasiums, the Philippine stick schools, the ring sports of Thailand and Myanmar.

categories.title: Martial arts of Europe, Africa and the Americas
categories.blurb: The wrestling and swordplay Europe wrote down in manuals, the stick and fist sports of Africa and Egypt, and the ring sports the Americas made out of both — up to the cage.
